text:
support_elaine: FYI some customers are hitting consistent 503s since the 10:15 canary rollout. Paging SREs. Customer ticket numbers: #C-8921, #C-8923. Graphs show a sharp spike exactly when the canary went live :eyes:

mike: Seeing the alert. P95 up and increased 5xx ratio. Any deploy info?

deploy-bot: deploy-redwood-service v2.14.6 started canary 2026-03-16T10:15:00Z by @anya (id: deploy-1763337000)

anya: I pushed the canary with a temporary flag to speed verification: `bypass_healthchecks=true` in the canary routing policy. It was intended to allow traffic to the new pool for warmup but I thought we scoped it to internal-only traffic.

mike: That flag can route traffic to instances that fail healthchecks -> possible cause of 503s. Where did the traffic tag get flipped?

anya: I validated locally but missed that the routing config uses `route_tag=public` for canaries. I set `bypass_healthchecks` at the deployment level not the internal test route. My bad.

sre-oncall: Ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale down canary to 0 traffic, 2) revert flag, 3) rollback to v2.14.5 if necessary. @anya can you patch the routing flag now?

anya: Patching now: ```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/redwood-service BYPASS_HEALTHCHECKS=false --overwrite
# or update config service-router -> canary.policy.bypass_healthchecks = false
```

mike: I'm also going to disable canary traffic in the router: ```
curl -X POST "https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/routes/canary/traffic" -d '{"percent":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ORCH_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

support_elaine: Customers still reporting 503s after the toggle, one provided headers for a failing request: `X-Request-ID: abc123`, `X-Proxy-Status: 503`, `X-Canary-Bypass: true`. That suggests some front proxies still honoring the bypass header.

mike: Good catch. We need to invalidate the prefix cache for proxies and restart the routing daemon on the public edge nodes. Doing rolling restart of route-proxy pods now: ```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart ds/route-proxy --selector=role=edge
```

deploy-bot: rollout restart started for ds/route-proxy at 2026-03-16T10:28:05Z

anya: I can confirm config was reverted in the control-plane. Will follow-up with a small smoke test: ```
curl -I "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# expecting 200, seeing 503 when hit edge with old prefix cache
```

sre-oncall: After restarts, 5xx rate is trending down. Team, leave canary at 0 traffic for now. We should run a replay in staging with the bypass flag set to understand why proxies kept honoring it even after config flip.

support_elaine: I've let the impacted customers know we're investigating and rolling back. Billing team asked if we should issue credit for the 10-20 minute outage window — queued to finance for review.

mike: Retro action items: (1) tighten deploy checklist so `bypass_healthchecks` can only be set on internal routes, (2) add a pre-rollout verifier that rejects routing flags that allow public traffic to bypass HC, (3) add quick rollback runbook link to deploy page.

anya: Sorry everyone — will own the postmortem and follow-up CLs for the verification step + docs.

sre-oncall: Thanks. If anyone sees resurgent 503s post-restart ping this thread and we'll re-open incident. Closing monitoring loop for now :white_check_mark:
